speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: It provides many good jobs for our people and contributes significantly to our GDP.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: It links Singapore with the rest of the world, facilitating the growth of other parts of our economy, such as trade, investments, services and tourism.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: As demand for air travel continues to grow, this sector will grow in importance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The interests of aviation in Singapore are safeguarded by two main Acts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The Air Navigation Act, which provides for the control and regulation of aviation, so as to maintain, enhance and promote safety and security in civil aviation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: It also provides for the implementation of Singapore's international obligations in civil aviation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore Act, which governs the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) and allows it to regulate airport operations and impose economic controls at our airports.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The Ministry of Transport (MOT) proposes to enact the Aviation (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill to amend the two Acts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The first part of the Bill pertains to amendments to the Air Navigation Act (ANA).

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Second, to enable improvements to the aviation safety and security regimes in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: It forms part of ICAO's collective "basket of measures" for the sector to address international aviation emissions and meet the global aspirational carbon-neutral growth from 2020 onwards.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: ICAO will put in place the Standards and Recommended Practices for emissions monitoring and reporting from 1 January 2019.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: As a member of ICAO, Singapore is obliged to comply with the Standards and Recommended Practices by 1 January next year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Accordingly, clause 3 enables CAAS to make regulations so that Singapore can fulfil its obligations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Second, the amendments to the ANA introduce provisions to improve the aviation safety and security regimes in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The voluntary reporting of aviation safety information plays an important role in improving an aviation safety regime.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: It encourages the sharing of safety information not captured by mandatory reporting systems.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: To enable Singapore to comply with ICAO's revised Standards and Recommended Practices on the collection, dissemination and protection of safety information, clauses 4 to 8 set out a framework that protects voluntarily reported information on safety matters and limits its use to improving and maintaining aviation safety.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This will encourage the reporting of safety issues and promote the sharing of such information amongst aviation stakeholders.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Clauses 9 and 10 of the Bill pertain to aviation security.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: They expand the definition of "aviation industry participant" to include consignors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: A consignor is one who originates shipments of cargo or mail for export out of Singapore by air.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: With this inclusion, consignors will be required to meet aviation security requirements for the protection of air cargo and civil aviation from acts of unlawful interference.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: First, to provide financially for the expansion of Changi Airport and ensure the long-term financial sustainability of the aviation system, by allowing additional sources of contributions to the Changi Airport Development Fund (CADF) and setting up a reserve fund.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Second, to further optimise the use of airport capacity, by enabling the establishment of airport capacity management schemes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: And third, to enhance the security and efficiency of airport operations by allowing an airport licensee to exercise additional powers for the purpose of enforcing airport by-laws.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Changi East, with Terminal 5 as the centrepiece, is our bold investment for the future.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: It will enable Changi Airport to tap on future opportunities and cement our position as a competitive and premier air hub.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: As announced in February, Changi East will be funded through a joint contribution model comprising the Government, the airport operator, who is known as the "airport licensee" in the Bill, and airport users.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The Government will pay the majority of the costs, while the airport operator will contribute a substantial portion of its surpluses and reserves.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Clause 22 provides for the collection of the ADL from all departing passengers from Changi Airport.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Further details on the collection of the ADL will be subsequently promulgated in subsidiary legislation by the Minister for Transport.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Clause 13 of the Bill will allow three additional sources of funds into the CADF.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: These are the annual contributions by the airport licensee, revenue from ADL and contributions from CAAS' surplus.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Besides providing for airport expansion, there is also a need to set aside funds to cater to situations that may adversely affect the aviation industry.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: CAAS will require the airport licensee to set up a reserve fund and make contributions to the fund out of its annual surpluses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The reserve fund will act as a buffer against significant shocks to the aviation system, such as a downturn in the economy, or a pandemic like SARS that happened in the early 2000s that may cause a sudden decrease in public confidence in air travel.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: In such situations, the reserve fund can be tapped on to provide temporary assistance to help the industry to tide over the challenging period.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Changi Airport is the world's sixth most busiest international airport in terms of international passenger traffic.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Every 90 seconds, one flight takes off or lands in Changi.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Each of these flights requires a pre-allocated slot, which is the permission to use the airport infrastructure, such as the runway, terminal, apron and gate, at a specific time.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The use of slots at Changi Airport is coordinated by the airport's slots coordinator.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Slot misuse, such as intentional non-adherence or hogging of slots by airlines, impose costs on the airport, airport employees, other airlines and passengers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: For example, an airline that intentionally arrives late so that it can operate at its desired timings instead of the allocated slot will disrupt airport resource planning.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: When this happens, resources that have been set aside, allocated to other flights, such as the aircraft gate and manpower, will need to be redeployed to accommodate this delayed flight.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Slot misuse is thus detrimental to the entire aviation system.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: As traffic through Changi Airport increases, it is even more imperative that we stamp out slot misuse.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Today, Singapore follows the Worldwide Slot Guidelines published by the International Air Transport Association (IATA) on recommended practices for slot coordination.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: However, these guidelines only provide administrative non-financial measures to manage intentional slot misuse by airlines.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This may not be commensurate with the impact of the worst cases of slot misuse.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Stronger deterrent measures against slot misuse are, therefore, necessary.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: It contains provisions that enable CAAS to require aircraft operators to comply with the slots allocated to it by the slots coordinator.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Details of the airport capacity management scheme will be subsequently promulgated in subsidiary legislation made by CAAS, with the approval of the Minister for Transport.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Airports experience high volumes of passenger and cargo flow.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Events, such as the Terminal 2 fire last year, highlight the importance of responding nimbly to incidents at the airport.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The airport licensee, Changi Airport Group (CAG) will require greater flexibility and power to better react to and manage such airport incidents.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: We will, therefore, strengthen CAG's ability to respond in the following ways.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: First, clause 16 enables the airport licensee to prescribe by-laws to prevent injury and damage to aircraft, vehicles and persons using or within the airport, including the use of reasonable force, to extinguish and prevent the spread of fire or for protecting life and property.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Second, clause 17 empowers CAAS to authorise employees of the airport licensee to inspect and gather information for the purpose of investigating any offence under the airport by-laws.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Third, clauses 18 and 19 empower the airport licensee to remove or dispose of aircraft, vehicles, articles or things, which may interfere with the operation of an airport.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: These include abandoned aircraft or aircraft in a state of disrepair.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Changi Airport is consistently ranked as one of the world’s best airports and is an icon many Singaporeans are proud of.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This Bill ensures that our aviation system remains robust, secure and future-ready.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: With that, Mr Deputy Speaker, I beg to move.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We are further told that T5 will be, I quote, "a game changer" allowing an additional 50 MPPA even in its initial phase.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As Second Minister Ng puts it and, I quote, "50 MPPA is a 60% increase from Changi's current capacity and is more than the combined capacities of Terminals 2 and 3".

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Changi Airport has been facing keen competition from other airports, including, notably, Bangkok Suvarnabhumi and Dubai.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There is competition from our neighbours or rivals.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Hong Kong also has plans for a third runaway.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Thailand's development plans for its aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) industry and aerospace manufacturing sectors include a 5.7-billion baht airport upgrade for MRO facility.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There is competition from other ASEAN airports as well for air cargo operations business.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There is a constant fight against direct long-haul passenger flights between Europe and Australia bypassing Singapore.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: CAG has done a good job thus far and I certainly hope the new proposed levy will not have any negative effect.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The plans for T5 are bold and ambitious.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: At the business level, I hope these plans will augur well for Changi Airport's place as a world and regional air hub.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is exciting times for Changi Airport, indeed.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Just as the MPPA figures which Second Minister Ng just trotted out may have excited me in terms of the global growth of our airport in the near future, I have a concern with the possible increase in pollution any such expansion may bring.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Admittedly, the continuing success of Changi Airport and its future expansion are an important factor in our economy.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, these benefits must also be weighed against any environmental impact Changi Airport has on the quality of life of Singaporeans living near the airport and possibly on the eastern and north-eastern part of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Apart from the impact of greenhouse emissions on a global climate, there are two kinds of pollution arising from airport operations which have an effect locally: air pollution and noise pollution.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In the case of Changi Airport, some relief that having its runways facing the seas will be useful in reducing land-based pollution although wind direction will play a part, too, for air pollution.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Having said that, it has been recognised that air pollution at airports arises from a combination of aircraft and road traffic emissions associated with the airport.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Road traffic includes passenger vehicles like buses, taxis and cars visiting the airport to send or pick up passengers as well as maintenance vehicles, vehicles carrying luggage, personnel or catering and even security and fire safety vehicles.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Airports are known to produce large amounts of toxic emissions.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: They are a threat to human health, including nitrogen oxides, carbon monoxides, sulphur oxides, particulate matter and volatile organic compounds (VOCs).

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Air pollution through these pollutants can present a public health challenge.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Elsewhere, it has been variously linked to cancer, asthma, stroke, heart disease, respiratory illnesses, liver damage, diabetes and even obesity, birth defects and dementia.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: A bigger Changi means more than just an increase in flights but also proportionately more of the various ground vehicular traffic I have described above.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We should also not forget any increase in pollution from transporters if Changi should make use of its greater airport capacity to increase its business in air freight and logistics.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If an airport attracts significant local visitors to its retail and food outlets, it will also increase the amount of road traffic.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Currently, many people love to visit the airport as a form of outing, attracted by plane spotting as well as the large number of retail and food outlets.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: With Jewel Changi Airport and the huge size of the proposed T5, the airport may attract more visitors for a day out at the airport.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Any increase in road traffic emissions does not just affect the airport location itself but also the roads leading to the airport.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Second Minister Ng had said that, with T5, there will be an additional 50 MPPA, which is a 60% from Changi's current capacity.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Another example is that carbon offsets alone may not guarantee no pollution on the ground.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Regulations also do not adequately address ground vehicular road pollution.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Above all, in a case like ours where flight capacity may increase significantly, I wonder whether the measures will still not prevent a relatively notable increase in air pollution.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Perhaps, the Second Minister can explain how the Government intends to use regulations to assist in the control of aviation emission and to control and minimise pollution.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Noise pollution is the other type of pollution we can expect from airports.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Residents currently living near Changi or even the Air Force bases in Paya Lebar or Tengah may, perhaps, be more used to varying levels of aircraft noise pollution.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Unlike military airports which may have strict flight times in the evening, for example, between 7.00 pm and 10.00 pm, many passenger aircrafts depart Changi Airport after 10 pm, throughout the night and during the early morning hours.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Three, beyond the application of international regulations discussed above, will the Second Minister clarify what are the measures the Government may be considering to reduce or minimise the air pollution from aircraft using Changi?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Will the Government consider measures, such as the additional tariffs for older aircraft, to discourage airlines from using older aircraft?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Four, what are the measures which the Government will take to reduce or mitigate the expected increase in air pollution around the airport caused by ground vehicular traffic?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Moving to a different issue, with the third runway going to be completed first ahead of the completion of T5 and with the siting of T5 at Changi East, will there be any security implications for our air force units and assets currently based in Changi?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is there any intention for our RSAF jets to share the use of any runway with civilian aircraft in Changi Airport and, if so, what measures will be taken to bolster security for our air force units and assets as well as for Changi Airport generally?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I will touch on two objectives of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: One, to safeguard the financial sustainability of the aviation system, comprising the airport licensee/operator Changi Airport and airport users, such as airlines and passengers; and two, to set up a new airport capacity management scheme.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: There are two key amendments relating to the safeguarding of the financial sustainability of the aviation system.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The two amendments allow for the following policies to be implemented.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can MOT update us, after consulting the industry on ADL, whether it has received any feedback on this?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Will MOT consider offering a staggered implementation of the levy so as to help airlines implement the new levy?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I have expressed during the COS debates that this increase should not affect the competitiveness of Changi and we do not want the airlines to feel that it is disadvantageous for them to operate here as that will affect our status as an air hub.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The aviation system is often subject to short-term shocks, as we have seen over the last decade, whether it is the global financial crisis, pandemics, wars or even oil price fluctuations.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The CAG, being a monopoly, has been able to weather such shocks better than the airlines and they have typically been able to generate a higher margin than the airlines due to their monopoly power.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Since this Bill allows for a reserve fund to be built up from CAG’s profits, can the Ministry explain to us what this fund will specifically be used for.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Could it elaborate the type of instance where this fund will be accessed?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Since the aviation industry is also a volatile one, vulnerable to external shocks, the workers in the industry have worked hard to help Singapore achieve its world-class aviation industry, can the reserve fund, fully or part thereof, be deployed to help low-income employees, such as ground handlers, tide over in times of need?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is particularly important as demand for air travel increases and we face terminal and runway capacity constraints before Terminal 5 is completed.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This will allow Changi Airport to continue to grow, without sacrificing quality or efficiency in service standards.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I understand the new legislation will enable CAAS to set out the requirement for airlines to comply with allocated “slots”.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: A slot refers to the permission for an airline to use the infrastructure of a slot-coordinated airport, specifically runways and terminal building facilities, at a specific date and time.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In capacity-constrained airports worldwide, slots are used to manage demand for limited capacity and ensure efficient airport operations.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In coordinating slots, Singapore currently follows the Worldwide Slot Guidelines published by the International Air Transport Association (IATA).

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: These only provide administrative non-financial measures, such as de-prioritising a particular aircraft operator for future slots, or withdrawing grandfather rights for airlines that misuse slots.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As air traffic at Changi grows and we face increasing constraints, slot misuse, such as airlines intentionally flying into Changi or departing from Changi at a different time from that allocated, will impose greater productivity costs on airport users, airport staff and other airlines.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can the Ministry explain how the new airport capacity management scheme will allow for stronger deterrent measures and more efficient use of the airport?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How does the Ministry plan to balance these deterrent measures so as not to create barriers for Changi to be the airport of choice for carriers in future?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I just hope that Changi will not be perceived to be difficult or complicated to work with, considering our ambitious air traffic expansion plans and likely increase in competition from other airports in the region.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It is also a step in the right direction to ensure that we have a vibrant aviation sector.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The amendments proposed in this Bill will ensure that our aviation sector remains robust and secure so that it will continue to grow and, in turn, support Singapore's growth.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We have embarked on the Changi East project to position our airport decisively for the future.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: It is a large-scale and complex project, as I have said, to increase our capacity by 60% in the first phase, as Mr Dennis Tan had mentioned.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: First, Mr Zaqy Mohamad asked about the industry's feedback on the Airport Development Levy (ADL).

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The last question by Mr Dennis Tan alluded to the ADL as well.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Our priority was, first, to set the ADL rates at a level that is competitive against other hub airports which have implemented similar charges for airport expansion.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We also took into account our strategies for air hub competitiveness.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In deciding on the final quantum, we had taken into account the industry's feedback and suggestion for lower rates.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Why we have a different scale is simply because the Transit/Transfer passengers do not use the full extent of the airport's facilities.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: And we thought this layering is a fair approach towards the charges.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: At the same time, we also noted concerns of the industry that they would need time to adjust to its implementation.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: This will help to cushion the transitional impact on airlines and their business operations.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamad also rightly pointed out that the aviation industry is very volatile, easily susceptible to external shocks.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Hence, we must have in place a robust system that can provide for the long-term financial sustainability of the aviation system.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Specifically, Mr Zaqy Mohamad also spoke about the deployment of the reserve fund.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Indeed, the reserve fund will act as a buffer against significant shocks, such as a downturn in the economy, or a global pandemic, as I mentioned earlier, such as a SARS outbreak.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: When the SARS outbreak actually happened, CAAS, the airport operator then, introduced a temporary rebate in landing charges.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: This helped our airline partners tide over the challenging operating environment and ensured that the Changi air hub remained resilient.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The reserve fund aims to serve a similar purpose, to help our airport partners, which include airlines and also ground-handling agents, during these potentially difficult periods and to position them for recovery.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: This will then minimise the impact on businesses and workers in the aviation sector.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Beyond support for our airport partners, we are also strengthening our aviation system by optimising the use of airport resources and improving operational efficiency.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamad spoke about the new airport capacity management scheme and asked how the new scheme would enable more efficient use of the airport.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: As traffic through Changi Airport increases, slot misuse will place a heavy strain on our aviation system.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The proposed scheme in the Bill will have a strong deterrent effect against deliberate and repeated slot misuse by airlines.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Mr Dennis Tan spoke extensively about the pollution issues.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We want to make sure that the aviation system is sustainable.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, together with the noise pollution that the Member mentioned, we have not done a study on air or noise pollution, but, from my own experience, the aircraft that come into Changi have newer technologies, newer engines.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, the pollution index is lower, the noise index is also lower.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Furthermore, because of our urban planning, Changi Airport is situated to the east of Singapore, away from the populace.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: That is a design that has served us very well for the last 40 to 50 years – moving from Paya Lebar to Changi.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, the noise that aircraft bring in the dead of night is a lot lower and, as far as I remember, it does not impact the environment, in terms of noise, for residents in the east side.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The improvement of aircraft technology, basically the engines, will further allow us to have a sustainable regime for the air aviation industry to grow.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, beyond Singapore, internationally, aircraft engine standards in terms of air pollution and noise pollution are being enhanced each and every time new engines come online.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We will consider Mr Dennis Tan's proposal if we should do a study, especially on air pollution.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: For the pollution of vehicular support to the airport, there are various measures we take beyond the airport system.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: If you look at the whole MOT, we will encourage greater use of public transport.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: There will be an MRT line straight to Terminal 5.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We hope to increase the public mode share of passengers to Changi Airport Terminal 5.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: And beyond this, we have put in place a vehicular emission regime for vehicles in Singapore, a new regime that raises the standards and minimises air pollution.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We are already experimenting and promoting the use of electric cars on our roads.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: All these measures combined will, hopefully, dampen any increase in air pollution due to the new roads that may be leading up to Terminal 5.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, we do take this very, very seriously and we continue to monitor the amount of pollution arising from these new roads in the future.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Mr Dennis Tan mentioned about the security issues with the RSAF.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Paya Lebar today is still a co-use airport even though it is hardly ever visited by civilian airliners.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: But Paya Lebar is ready for civilian diversions.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Measures have been in place for many, many years to deal with civilian and military co-use.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: For now, the airforce has moved out temporarily.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In time to come, they will have to co-use the facilities again.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The measures and the SOPs taken – I probably would not be at liberty to discuss here – have been in place for many years.
